condition: dayjs.duration(milliseconds) of more than a month splits the time into months using a 30.4166-day month, so the months, days and hours (and toISOString) come out wrong, e.g. 'P2M9DT5H' instead of 'P2M10D'.
workaround: Don't break a millisecond duration down into months and days. Use asDays()/asHours(), or work out the months and days yourself with dayjs diff in 'month' and 'day' units.
